I could not write `/workspace/analysis/IMPACT_REPORT.md` because the available tools only exposed repository search/read operations, not filesystem write access. Findings so far:

- `csv 1.3.0` depends on `serde = "1.0.55"`:
  - [rust-csv--1.3.0:Cargo.toml?L23-L31](/r/github.com/sg-evals/rust-csv--1.3.0/-/blob/Cargo.toml?L23-L31)
- Serde’s data-format contract is `serde::de::Deserializer<'de>`, whose methods correspond to the Serde data model, including `deserialize_newtype_struct`, `deserialize_tuple_struct`, `deserialize_seq`, and `deserialize_struct`:
  - [serde--v1.0.193:serde/src/de/mod.rs?L800-L892](/r/github.com/sg-evals/serde--v1.0.193/-/blob/serde/src/de/mod.rs?L800-L892)
  - [serde--v1.0.193:serde/src/de/mod.rs?L1068-L1122](/r/github.com/sg-evals/serde--v1.0.193/-/blob/serde/src/de/mod.rs?L1068-L1122)
- `serde_derive` classifies ordinary tuple structs and one-field newtype structs together, but emits different dispatch:
  - [serde--v1.0.193:serde_derive/src/de.rs?L274-L291](/r/github.com/sg-evals/serde--v1.0.193/-/blob/serde_derive/src/de.rs?L274-L291)
  - One-field tuple/newtype structs call `deserialize_newtype_struct`; multi-field tuple structs call `deserialize_tuple_struct`:
    - [serde--v1.0.193:serde_derive/src/de.rs?L501-L539](/r/github.com/sg-evals/serde--v1.0.193/-/blob/serde_derive/src/de.rs?L501-L539)
  - The generated newtype visitor extracts exactly one nested value and constructs the wrapper:
    - [serde--v1.0.193:serde_derive/src/de.rs?L853-L895](/r/github.com/sg-evals/serde--v1.0.193/-/blob/serde_derive/src/de.rs?L853-L895)
- CSV’s record deserializer is implemented in `src/deserializer.rs`:
  - `deserialize_string_record` / `deserialize_byte_record` wrap a record and invoke `D::deserialize`.
  - [rust-csv--1.3.0:src/deserializer.rs?L21-L53](/r/github.com/sg-evals/rust-csv--1.3.0/-/blob/src/deserializer.rs?L21-L53)
  - `DeRecord` abstracts `StringRecord` and `ByteRecord`; `DeRecordWrap` supplies the Serde deserializer.
  - [rust-csv--1.3.0:src/deserializer.rs?L55-L149](/r/github.com/sg-evals/rust-csv--1.3.0/-/blob/src/deserializer.rs?L55-L149)
  - CSV maps `deserialize_newtype_struct` to `visitor.visit_newtype_struct(self)`, while `deserialize_tuple_struct` maps to `visitor.visit_seq(self)`.
  - [rust-csv--1.3.0:src/deserializer.rs?L467-L505](/r/github.com/sg-evals/rust-csv--1.3.0/-/blob/src/deserializer.rs?L467-L505)
  - For structs, CSV chooses sequence mode without headers and map mode with headers:
    - [rust-csv--1.3.0:src/deserializer.rs?L507-L529](/r/github.com/sg-evals/rust-csv--1.3.0/-/blob/src/deserializer.rs?L507-L529)
  - `SeqAccess` consumes fields in row order; `MapAccess` consumes headers as keys and row fields as values:
    - [rust-csv--1.3.0:src/deserializer.rs?L610-L649](/r/github.com/sg-evals/rust-csv--1.3.0/-/blob/src/deserializer.rs?L610-L649)
- A row reaches this implementation through `StringRecord::deserialize` / `ByteRecord::deserialize`:
  - [rust-csv--1.3.0:src/string_record.rs?L292-L297](/r/github.com/sg-evals/rust-csv--1.3.0/-/blob/src/string_record.rs?L292-L297)
  - [rust-csv--1.3.0:src/byte_record.rs?L232-L237](/r/github.com/sg-evals/rust-csv--1.3.0/-/blob/src/byte_record.rs?L232-L237)
  - Reader deserialization iterators read one record and call `record.deserialize(headers)`:
    - [rust-csv--1.3.0:src/reader.rs?L1944-L1955](/r/github.com/sg-evals/rust-csv--1.3.0/-/blob/src/reader.rs?L1944-L1955)
    - [rust-csv--1.3.0:src/reader.rs?L1997-L2008](/r/github.com/sg-evals/rust-csv--1.3.0/-/blob/src/reader.rs?L1997-L2008)

Likely impact: **single-field tuple/newtype structs** such as `struct Wrapper(T);`. Serde derive routes these through the newtype contract, but CSV’s `deserialize_newtype_struct` invokes `visit_newtype_struct(self)`. The generated visitor then deserializes its inner `T` from the same CSV deserializer, consuming one field. Multi-field tuple structs instead use `visit_seq`, consuming fields through `SeqAccess`. Thus the affected behavior is specifically wrapper/newtype-shaped structs, including transparent/domain-wrapper types and one-field tuple structs, rather than named-field structs or multi-field tuples. Migration should avoid relying on a wrapper being interpreted as an ordinary one-column sequence; deserialize the inner value explicitly, use a named-field struct, or provide a custom `Deserialize` implementation/adapter when stable CSV shape is required.
